context_pill: Diversion of Income by Overriding Title
example_summary: MKG Agency's obligation to pay 20% of profits to the mother constitutes a diversion of income by overriding title, excluding the amount from the firm's taxable income.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Doctrine / Concept | Statutory Provision | Core Legal Condition | Tax Treatment & Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Diversion of Income by Overriding Title** | Section 4 | Creation of a legal charge or obligation prior to the receipt by the assessee | Amount does not form part of the total income of the recipient entity; excluded at source |
| **Application of Income** | Section 4 | Obligation arising after the income has reached and vested in the assessee | Amount forms part of total income; no deduction allowed unless specifically provided under PGBP |


> [!IMPORTANT] Core Judicial Benchmark:
> As established in landmark jurisprudence (e.g., *CIT vs. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons*), if an overriding title diverts income before it becomes the assessee's income, the assessee receives it merely on behalf of the rightful claimant.


> [!WARNING] Statutory Trap:
> Contractual application of profits or voluntary diversion of post-receipt income by a partnership deed or agreement does not amount to diversion by overriding title; such amounts are taxable in the hands of the entity and constitute mere application of income.

director.justification: The core legal issue is classifying the payment as either a 'Diversion of Income by Overriding Title' or an 'Application of Income' based on the timing of the legal obligation.
director.visual_metaphor: A pipeline with a pre-installed diversion valve that redirects water before it reaches the main reservoir.
